transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

A lazy yellow flame that makes soot means the gas is not burning cleanly. The commonest cause is the back burner cap or crown being greasy, damp, blocked or slightly out of position; less commonly, the burner’s air/gas supply or injector needs professional attention. Do not keep using that burner while it is sooting, as it can coat pans and indicates incomplete combustion. With the hob cool and switched off, remove the cap and crown, wash and dry them thoroughly, clear visible debris from the flame holes without poking anything that could enlarge them, and refit them flat and correctly aligned. If it is still yellow and sooty afterwards, stop using that burner and arrange a Gas Safe registered engineer to inspect it.

Thank you, I'll have a look at the cap. I should mention that I've also noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. Does that change anything?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Burner cap/crown is dirty, wet or not seated correctly, disturbing the gas-air mix (high)
Blocked burner ports or air inlet causing incomplete combustion (medium)
Gas supply, injector or burner valve fault requiring an engineer (low)

reading.symptom: Back burner has a lazy yellow flame and leaves black soot on pans

plan: They asked: "What's wrong with it?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "Back burner has a lazy yellow flame and leaves black soot on pans". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
